articles.headline: RBI board approves record ₹2.11 lakh crore dividend for the government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India approved a record surplus transfer of ₹2.11 lakh crore to the central government for FY24. This amount is more than double the government's budgeted target of ₹1.02 lakh crore, providing a major fiscal boost for infrastructure spending and deficit reduction.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets hit record highs following RBI dividend announcement
articles.summary: The Sensex and Nifty 50 reached all-time highs as investors cheered the RBI's record dividend payout. The Sensex jumped 268 points to close at a new peak, while the Nifty gained 68 points, reflecting optimism about the government's improved fiscal position and potential for increased spending.

articles.headline: IndiGo Q4 net profit jumps 106% to ₹1,895 crore on strong demand
articles.summary: InterGlobe Aviation reported a net profit of ₹1,894.8 crore for the quarter ended March 2024, supported by robust passenger growth and higher yields. The airline's revenue from operations rose 26% year-on-year to ₹17,825 crore, marking its sixth consecutive profitable quarter.

articles.headline: Spain, Ireland, and Norway announce formal recognition of Palestinian state
articles.summary: In a coordinated diplomatic move, Spain, Ireland, and Norway announced they will formally recognize a Palestinian state on May 28. The leaders stated the decision aims to support a two-state solution and promote peace in the region, while Israel recalled its ambassadors in protest.

articles.headline: IMD issues severe heatwave red alert for Delhi and neighboring states
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert for Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan as temperatures crossed 47 degrees Celsius. The severe heatwave is expected to continue for several days, prompting warnings about heat-related illnesses and power demand spikes.

articles.headline: Net direct tax collections for FY24 rise 18% to ₹19.58 lakh crore
articles.summary: India's net direct tax collections for the fiscal year 2023-24 reached ₹19.58 lakh crore, surpassing the government's revised estimates. The growth was driven by a 17.7% increase in personal income tax collections and a rise in corporate tax payments, indicating strong economic activity.

articles.headline: JSW Steel reports 64% drop in Q4 profit amid higher costs
articles.summary: JSW Steel's consolidated net profit fell to ₹1,299 crore for the March quarter, down from ₹3,664 crore a year earlier. The decline was attributed to elevated raw material prices and lower domestic steel realizations despite a significant increase in sales volume.

articles.headline: BHEL consolidated net profit declines 25% to ₹489.6 crore in Q4
articles.summary: State-run Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited reported a 25.6% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit for the fourth quarter. While revenue stayed relatively flat at ₹8,260 crore, increased raw material expenses and operational costs weighed on the bottom line.

articles.headline: Awfis Space Solutions IPO sees 2x subscription on opening day
articles.summary: The initial public offering of coworking firm Awfis Space Solutions was subscribed 2.02 times on its first day of bidding. The retail portion was subscribed 6 times, while the non-institutional investors' category saw 2.7 times subscription, showing strong interest in the flex-workspace sector.

articles.headline: UK inflation rate falls to 2.3% hitting lowest level since 2021
articles.summary: British consumer price inflation dropped to 2.3% in April, down from 3.2% in March. This marks the lowest inflation rate in three years, bringing it close to the Bank of England's 2% target and raising expectations for potential interest rate cuts later this year.

articles.headline: Global markets cautious as investors await Nvidia quarterly earnings results
articles.summary: World stocks remained steady as traders prepared for Nvidia’s first-quarter results. The chipmaker's earnings are viewed as a critical barometer for the artificial intelligence sector, which has been the primary driver of the global equity market rally over the past year.

articles.headline: KKR crushes Sunrisers Hyderabad to enter IPL 2024 final
articles.summary: Kolkata Knight Riders secured a spot in the IPL final with an 8-wicket victory over Sunrisers Hyderabad in Qualifier 1. Mitchell Starc’s three-wicket burst early in the game helped bowl out SRH for 159, a target KKR chased down in just 13.4 overs.

articles.headline: Yogi Adityanath to remain CM face for upcoming Uttar Pradesh polls
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath confirmed he will lead the BJP's campaign in the next state assembly elections. While Deputy CM Maurya stated a final call would be taken after the polls, Adityanath emphasized that the party's symbol is the 'lotus' and he remains the primary face. The statements come as BJP leaders prepare for the 2027 contest against the SP-led alliance.

articles.headline: Survey shows 80% of Agniveers wanted to stay before scheme revamp
articles.summary: An internal survey conducted by the Indian Armed Forces revealed that roughly 80% of the first batch of Agniveers wished to continue their service beyond four years. This data was collected before the government announced a major revamp of the Agnipath scheme, which now seeks to retain 75% of recruits instead of the original 25%. The change aims to address long-term personnel requirements.

articles.headline: MCD to repair collapsed 160-year-old Town Hall in Delhi within 3 months
articles.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has announced plans to repair and restore the iconic 160-year-old Town Hall in Chandni Chowk within three months. A portion of the Grade-I heritage building had recently collapsed. The restoration will follow a detailed standard operating procedure to preserve its original character and historical significance as a major civic landmark.

articles.headline: Over 331,000 new voter applications filed as Delhi special summary revision ends
articles.summary: The office of the Chief Electoral Officer in Delhi received over 331,000 applications for voter inclusion as the Special Summary Revision phase concluded. While there were over 35,000 requests for deletion, the net addition indicates significant interest ahead of polls. The final electoral roll is scheduled for publication in early January following a verification period.

articles.headline: Leatherback turtle nesting in Nicobar drops significantly, WII report reveals
articles.summary: A study by the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) has reported a decline in the number of Leatherback turtle nests at Galathea Bay in the Nicobar Islands. The count dropped from 634 in 2022-23 to 478 in 2024-25. Experts suggest that regional environmental changes and potential habitat disturbances from coastal development projects may be contributing to the reduced nesting activity.

articles.headline: US deported 1,700 Indians in 2024 amid crackdown on illegal immigration
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that the US government has deported approximately 1,700 Indian nationals so far in 2024. This move is part of an intensified crackdown on undocumented immigrants. The MEA stated it is working with US authorities to facilitate the legal return and ensure the welfare of individuals caught in the expanded deportation sweeps across North America.

articles.headline: Japan and India unveil Lupex rover for joint lunar water hunt mission
articles.summary: Japan's space agency, JAXA, has unveiled a prototype of the rover developed for the Lunar Polar Exploration (Lupex) mission, a joint venture with India's ISRO. The mission, scheduled for 2028, aims to explore the moon's south pole for water ice. The rover is designed to navigate permanently shadowed regions and gather data on the quantity and quality of potential water resources.

articles.headline: India's sugar production projected to fall 15% due to weather conditions
articles.summary: The Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) has projected a 15% decline in sugar production for the 2024-25 season, estimating output at 26.5 million tonnes. The dip is attributed to unfavorable weather conditions in major producing states like Maharashtra and Karnataka. This reduction may impact domestic prices and export quotas as stocks remain tight globally.

articles.headline: Meta reports spike in content takedowns in India during early 2026
articles.summary: Meta's transparency report revealed a significant increase in content takedowns in India during the first half of 2026. Over 5 million pieces of content were removed or restricted on Facebook and Instagram, a sharp rise from 70,000 in 2025. The company cited its efforts to comply with local regulations and address automated misinformation as primary reasons for the spike in enforcement.

articles.headline: Delhi to add 1,800+ hospital beds with two new government facilities
articles.summary: The Delhi government has announced that two new state-run hospitals will open next year, adding over 1,800 beds to the city's healthcare infrastructure. These facilities, located in Siraspur and Hastsal, are intended to provide specialized medical care and reduce the burden on existing hospitals. The initiative is part of a broader plan to strengthen public health services in the Capital.

articles.headline: CDSCO flags 324 drug samples as not of standard quality in October
articles.summary: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) has identified 324 drug samples as 'Not of Standard Quality' (NSQ) in its latest monthly report for October. The flagged medicines include various antibiotics and common medications from several pharmaceutical companies. The regulator has issued alerts to ensure these batches are withdrawn from the market to protect public health.

articles.headline: Ukraine says it struck major Russian airbase, hitting five planes
articles.summary: The Ukrainian military claims to have successfully struck a major Russian airbase, resulting in damage to at least five aircraft. The long-range drone strike targeted infrastructure used for launching aerial attacks on Ukrainian cities. While Russia has not confirmed the extent of the damage, the incident marks another significant escalation in the ongoing cross-border conflict.

articles.headline: Ben Stokes and Aaryavir Sehwag register for upcoming IPL mega auction
articles.summary: England all-rounder Ben Stokes and Aaryavir Sehwag, son of Virender Sehwag, have registered for the Indian Premier League (IPL) mega auction. A total of 1,220 players have signed up for the event scheduled for December. Stokes' participation adds star power to the pool, while Aaryavir represents a new generation of talent entering the league for the first time.

articles.headline: India Pavilion wins prestigious award at Venice Biennale for cultural display
articles.summary: The India Pavilion at the Venice Biennale has been honored with a top award for its exhibition. The display, which showcases contemporary Indian art and traditional influences, was lauded for its creativity and depth. This recognition highlights India's growing influence and presence in the global contemporary art scene, celebrating the fusion of traditional craft and modern expression.

articles.headline: India must focus on reaping AI gains, says Palo Alto chairman
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks chairman Nikesh Arora says India should focus on AI diffusion and adoption rather than building expensive frontier models. He notes that building models is a high-investment game currently dominated by the US and China. India's large population offers a major opportunity to democratize healthcare and education through AI adoption without massive frontier spending.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav to release Samajwadi Party manifesto for UP elections
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav will release the 'Jana Mana Ghoshna' manifesto for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The document focuses on women, youth, and the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) outreach. Key promises include annual pensions of Rs 40,000 for women and 300 units of free power for domestic consumers.

articles.headline: GAIL plans data centre entry through equal joint venture partnership
articles.summary: GAIL (India) plans to enter the data centre industry by leveraging its nationwide optic fibre network and land banks. The state-run company is seeking a strategic partner for an equal joint venture to build its first 5 MW facility in Faridabad. Future expansions are planned across Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra based on the success of the first unit.

articles.headline: Rising inflation across goods and services increases chances of rate hike
articles.summary: RBI’s November bulletin shows that a larger proportion of goods and services breached the 4% inflation threshold in October. Headline retail inflation hit 6.09%, exceeding the central bank's upper tolerance limit. The data builds a case for potential interest rate hikes in the upcoming December policy review to manage broad-based price pressures.

articles.headline: Noel Tata opposes Tata Sons EGM and N Chandrasekaran's reappointment
articles.summary: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has opposed a proposed extraordinary general meeting of Tata Sons, arguing the firm cannot pursue an IPO without first becoming a public company. He also challenged the validity of a board resolution regarding executive chairman N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, citing the lack of required affirmative votes under Article 121.

articles.headline: Centre considers special voting rights to retain control in PFC-REC merger
articles.summary: The government is considering issuing special shares with enhanced voting privileges to maintain majority control in the merged PFC-REC entity. The proposal involves adding 80.6 million superior voting rights shares. This would allow the Centre to hold 51% voting control despite holding only a 51.75% equity stake in the merged power-sector financier.

articles.headline: Lenders issue auction notices as gold prices drop below LTV limits
articles.summary: Gold finance companies are issuing legal auction notices as falling gold prices caused nearly 40% of portfolios to breach loan-to-value (LTV) limits. Lenders have triggered margin calls, asking borrowers for additional collateral or partial repayment. In response, banks and NBFCs have lowered LTV on fresh loans to 60-65% to provide a larger cushion.

articles.headline: J&K Police identify 35 terrorists operating from Pakistan to revive militancy
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir DGP Nalin Prabhat stated that 35 terrorists from Reasi district have exfiltrated to Pakistan to work for Hizbul Mujahideen. Police have attached 28.8 kanals of land belonging to five such individuals. The suspects are allegedly selling properties to finance terror activities and radicalize youth in the Union Territory.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues notice to Delhi Police on Umar Khalid's bail
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice to Delhi Police on fresh bail pleas filed by activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. The bench declined interim bail at this stage, citing the need to hear the police first. Khalid has been in incarceration for over six years under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

articles.headline: Supreme Court defers corruption trial of former minister Senthil Balaji
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the trial court to defer proceedings in the cash-for-jobs corruption case involving former Tamil Nadu minister Senthil Balaji until mid-December. The bench noted that while the allegations are serious, the trial should not be rushed. Balaji’s defense highlighted that the alleged offenses date back to 2021 and 2022.

articles.headline: PhonePe restarts IPO talks seeking a valuation up to 1.4 lakh crore
articles.summary: Digital payments firm PhonePe has resumed discussions with bankers to launch an initial public offering worth Rs 12,000–14,000 crore. The issue is expected to be an entirely offer-for-sale. The move follows improved market sentiment and PhonePe's expectation to turn profit-after-tax positive in the first half of the year, following a net loss in FY26.

articles.headline: Rupee appreciation threatens to hit Indian IT company operating margins
articles.summary: Kotak Institutional Equities warns that the rupee's recent appreciation against the US dollar could reduce IT services operating margins by 50-70 basis points. The currency gains seen in FY26 are being reversed as the rupee strengthens. This adds pressure alongside AI-led pricing changes and limited high-margin AI revenue for major firms like TCS and Infosys.

articles.headline: PayU India reports 12 million dollar adjusted Ebitda profit for H1
articles.summary: PayU India achieved an adjusted Ebitda profit of $12 million for the first half of fiscal 2027, driven by its credit business. Although half-yearly revenue dipped 3% to $384 million due to merchant exits, the company expects full-year revenue to grow 17-18%. It targets a total profit-after-tax of Rs 50-60 crore for the year and a doubling of its FY26 Ebitda.

articles.headline: Former Zomato executive Rakesh Ranjan appointed as Uber India head
articles.summary: Uber has selected former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan to lead its India and South Asia operations. Ranjan, who currently works at Allen Online, is expected to join in January. He replaces Prabhjeet Singh, who left to join OpenAI. This is Uber's first external appointment for its India head in over a decade as it faces competition in ride-hailing.

articles.headline: IT Secretary defends Sarvam AI's use of open-weight global models
articles.summary: IT Secretary S Krishnan supported AI startup Sarvam's 'Token Factory' service, stating there is no evidence of subsidy misuse. Sarvam faced criticism for offering global open-weight models, including Chinese ones. Krishnan noted that the government uses similar harness-based services to prevent domestic data leaks and that there is no shortage of chips for Indian ideas.

articles.headline: Electric tractor maker Autonxt seeks 15 million dollars in fresh funding
articles.summary: Mumbai-based electric tractor manufacturer Autonxt Automation is raising $15 million to expand its product portfolio and scale manufacturing. The capital will be used to develop higher horsepower models and standalone electric loaders for industrial sectors like construction and mining. The company currently has a manufacturing unit in Uttar Pradesh.

articles.headline: US-based VU Venture Partners to increase startup investments in India
articles.summary: VC firm VU Venture Partners is expanding its India presence, planning to invest $100,000 to $1 million in early-stage startups. The firm, which has backed OpenAI and SpaceX, will focus on deeptech, space tech, and robotics. It also uses its Venture University program to train a new pool of venture capital investors within the Indian startup ecosystem.

articles.headline: Raise Financial Services to invest 100 crore in AI platform TradingCharts
articles.summary: Raise Financial Services, parent of Dhan, is committing Rs 100 crore to scale TradingCharts, an AI-powered stock analytics platform. Currently used by 50,000 daily traders, the tool allows users to create custom indicators. Raise plans to open the platform to other brokerages in the coming months after more than a year of internal development.

articles.headline: Indian markets defy Asia-Pacific selloff to surge 2 percent
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 and Sensex surged nearly 2% to fresh FY27 peaks, ignoring a broader selloff in Asian markets like Japan and South Korea. The rally was driven by resilient corporate earnings and global capital rotating from AI-driven markets to India. Foreign investors have poured a record $14.3 billion into Indian equities in November, supporting the recovery.

articles.headline: Rupee recovers entire fiscal year losses on strong foreign inflows
articles.summary: The Indian rupee erased its year-to-date losses, closing at 92.24 against the US dollar. The currency has recovered over 5% from its record low of 96.96 in May. The bounce is attributed to record monthly foreign institutional inflows of over $14 billion into Indian equities, making it a top-performing emerging market currency this quarter.

articles.headline: Gujarat overtakes Maharashtra as state with most active individual investors
articles.summary: Gujarat has become the state with the largest pool of active individual investors in India, accounting for 19% of the total base. According to NSE data, Gujarat had 2.81 million active investors in October, surpassing Maharashtra's 2.3 million. Uttar Pradesh ranked third with a 10.1% share of active participants as total unique investors reached 14.4 million.

articles.headline: Public sector banks face lending slowdown as surplus liquidity fades
articles.summary: Public sector banks (PSBs) may struggle to maintain aggressive loan growth as their liquidity edge over private lenders diminishes. The loan-to-deposit ratio gap has narrowed significantly since FY20. Bernstein reports that PSBs have used much of their balance-sheet headroom, while private banks continue to protect their deposit shares despite losing ground in lending.

articles.headline: Deutsche Bank and PNB partner to finance corporate acquisitions in India
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank and Punjab National Bank have signed an agreement to structure and finance corporate acquisitions. The alliance leverages RBI reforms allowing domestic lenders to fund up to 75% of deal values for listed and unlisted firms. The partnership aims to support Indian companies as they grow in scale and pursue international strategic ambitions.

articles.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp shares rally 25 percent on strong earnings and outlook
articles.summary: Poonawalla Fincorp's stock has gained over 25% since October, driven by improved lending yields and better asset quality. The company's September quarter performance showed a net profit increase to Rs 375 crore. Brokerages have raised price targets to Rs 600-625, citing moderating credit costs and increasing benefits from operating leverage in its digital loan segments.

articles.headline: India's satellite sector hampered by heavy reliance on imported components
articles.summary: A report by IN-SPACe reveals that India's satellite manufacturing sector remains vulnerable due to dependence on imported semiconductors and specialized materials. Nearly 60% of satellite costs are linked to imported parts. The regulator calls for common-use test centers and domestic supplier development to help reach a projected $44 billion market by 2033.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry to track infrastructure projects with cost overruns above 10%
articles.summary: The finance ministry has sought detailed explanations for cost escalations exceeding 10% on capital and infrastructure projects above Rs 5 crore. No enhanced budget will be allocated without justification for delays and revised timelines. This follows data showing Rs 3.22 lakh crore in cost overruns for 1,853 large projects above Rs 150 crore.

articles.headline: Deeptech startup Red Balloon to launch second near-space mission in December
articles.summary: Vijayawada-based startup Red Balloon Aerospacial will launch its second mission, 'AURA', from Amaravati in December. The project features a super-pressure balloon and a tethered aerostat to develop commercial applications in the underutilised near-space region. The company aims to explore research and ascent capabilities for communications and observation.

articles.headline: Eastman Exports to set up 266 crore smart garment factory in AP
articles.summary: Tirupur-based Eastman Exports is investing Rs 266 crore to build its first smart garment manufacturing facility in Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh. The project is expected to create 4,500 jobs across three units. The factory will use modern technology and automated processes to manufacture knitted and woven garments, with commercial production starting in April 2027.

articles.headline: Air passenger service prices surge 35.5 percent in second quarter
articles.summary: Data for the Service Producer Price Index shows air passenger service prices grew 35.5% year-on-year in the July-September quarter. Banking service prices declined nearly 4%, while railway passenger services rose 2.2%. The index, using 2022-23 as a base, aims to measure price movements at the provider level across seven key sectors including telecom and insurance.

articles.headline: Over 1200 players register for IPL 2027 player auction in Goa
articles.summary: A total of 1,220 players, including 939 Indians and 281 overseas cricketers, have registered for the IPL 2027 auction scheduled for December 16 in Goa. There are 66 available slots, including 25 for overseas players. Registrations include stars from 18 countries, with Australia and South Africa leading overseas entries with 53 and 40 players respectively.

articles.headline: Bengal to adopt new land pooling policy for faster industrialization
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced a 'middle-of-the-road' land policy to support industry without forceful acquisition. The state will adopt land pooling methods similar to those in Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh. Adhikari promised fixed timelines for approvals and incentives up to 120% for plant and machinery investments.

articles.headline: Adani Group to bid for thermal power and ropeway projects in Bengal
articles.summary: Karan Adani, MD of Adani Ports, announced plans to bid for thermal power projects and the Kolkata Outer Ring Road. The group aims to invest over Rs 1 lakh crore in West Bengal by 2035. Adani highlighted the strategic importance of eastern India's mineral wealth and the group's intent to export energy products to Europe via its Dutch storage acquisition.

articles.headline: ITC to expand Bengal footprint in tourism and food processing sectors
articles.summary: ITC Chairman Sanjiv Puri announced expansion plans for West Bengal, focusing on value-added agriculture, hospitality, and sustainable packaging. The conglomerate is targeting a Rs 20,000 crore nationwide expansion. Puri emphasized that operating productively in Bengal is possible by aligning human capital and local resources with a long-term corporate vision.

articles.headline: Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta pledges predictable policy regime for West Bengal
articles.summary: State Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta aims to restore investor confidence through predictable policies and power subsidies. He highlighted the upcoming abolition of the Urban Land Ceiling Act as a key trigger for a real estate boom. Dasgupta noted that managing the state’s Rs 8 lakh crore debt requires better compliance rather than tax hikes.

articles.headline: West Bengal to develop vertical industrial parks to address land scarcity
articles.summary: Subrata Gupta, adviser to the CM, stated that Bengal will adopt a vertical development model for industry to generate employment despite land density challenges. The state plans to offer plug-and-play facilities in industrial parks. Currently, West Bengal accounts for 7.5% of investment intentions in India but faces low realization rates on actual ground projects.

articles.headline: Industry leaders urge West Bengal to attract global capability centres
articles.summary: Experts at the Bengal Ascends summit highlighted that West Bengal needs to strengthen its tech ecosystem to attract the next wave of Global Capability Centres (GCCs). Shalini Pillay of KPMG noted that the state's diaspora could be a key asset for talent. Sangita Singh of Everforth emphasized a 60% cost advantage for engineering hubs in the state compared to other cities.

articles.headline: Panel recommends using GST and corporate records for accurate GDP data
articles.summary: A government-appointed panel proposed using state-wise GST returns and corporate expenditure records to improve gross domestic product (GDP) estimates. The committee, chaired by Ravindra Dholakia, suggests moving away from fixed ratios to direct administrative data. This aim is to enhance the reliability of state and district-level economic accounts across most industries.

articles.headline: PepsiCo India to build 868 crore food manufacturing plant in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: PepsiCo India is investing Rs 868 crore to establish a greenfield snacks manufacturing plant in Tamil Nadu. The facility will produce Lay’s and Kurkure brands to serve southern Indian markets. This project is part of a larger Rs 5,700 crore investment plan through 2030 and is expected to create 650 direct and indirect jobs while supporting local ancillary industries.

articles.headline: Indian pharmaceutical exports grow 5.7 percent to 18.89 billion dollars
articles.summary: India's pharmaceutical exports rose to $18.89 billion during April-October, led by drug formulations and biologicals. Bulk drug exports grew over 14%. The US remains the largest destination, though shipments to the country declined 2%. Meanwhile, imports grew 3%, with China remaining the primary source, accounting for over 36% of India's total pharma imports.

articles.headline: Coca-Cola to relaunch iconic Gold Spot brand as low-sugar beverage
articles.summary: Coca-Cola India is bringing back the orange carbonated brand Gold Spot after a 26-year hiatus. The relaunch targets a new generation of consumers with a low-sugar formulation. Coca-Cola acquired the brand from Parle Bisleri in 1993 along with Thums Up and Limca. The move comes as competition intensifies in the sparkling flavors category.

articles.headline: P&G Home Products reports subdued 3.4 percent revenue growth in FY26
articles.summary: Procter & Gamble Home Products saw revenue rise 3.4% to Rs 9,359 crore in fiscal 2026, while net profit fell 2.7%. The company faced challenges from intense competition and soft urban consumption. Across its three Indian entities, combined revenue reached Rs 16,749 crore, with growth driven largely by its listed businesses which saw stronger earnings.

articles.headline: UnitedHealth Group leases 4.3 lakh square feet office space in Chennai
articles.summary: US healthcare major UnitedHealth Group has leased over 4.34 lakh square feet of office space at Embassy Splendid Tech Zone in Chennai. The five-year lease, starting at a monthly rent of Rs 69.8 per sq ft, marks a significant expansion for the company's Optum business in India. The lease includes a 15% rental escalation every three years and commences in December.

articles.headline: Foxconn claims Indian vendor breached contract over dormitory rental dispute
articles.summary: Foxconn stated that BCD Emprassa, a vendor providing dormitory housing in Bengaluru, failed to meet contractual obligations. The clarification follows a report that the vendor moved the NCLT to recover $15 million in unpaid dues. Foxconn alleges the dispute stems from the supplier’s failure to maintain quality standards and corrective actions despite repeated requests.

articles.headline: State and central laboratories flag over 300 drug samples as poor quality
articles.summary: Drugs testing laboratories across India flagged 287 samples as 'not of standard quality' (NSQ) in October, while central labs identified 37. The findings are part of routine regulatory surveillance by the CDSCO. The list of substandard and spurious drugs is being displayed on the national regulator's portal to inform the public and improve compliance in the pharma industry.

articles.headline: Navi Mumbai International Airport handles 40 lakh passengers in 11 months
articles.summary: The Navi Mumbai International Airport reached a milestone of 40 lakh passengers within 11 months of starting operations. The facility handled over 41 lakh total passengers, with domestic travel accounting for nearly 40.9 lakh. The airport is rapidly integrating into the Mumbai Metropolitan Region's aviation ecosystem, with nearly equal numbers of arriving and departing travelers.

articles.headline: AI agents to force Indian IT firms to rethink business models
articles.summary: Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke says Indian IT firms must focus on the economics of AI deployment rather than just coding talent. He warns that poorly managed AI token costs could eat into productivity gains. Dohmke believes AI makes the traditional software development lifecycle obsolete, requiring developers to oversee autonomous agents functioning as experts for their customers.

articles.headline: Companies linked to Alice Huang financed 270 million dollar AI servers
articles.summary: Financial records show that businesses connected to Alice Huang helped finance $270 million worth of AI servers for data centers in China. The hardware was linked to a project involving Tencent. The findings come as US authorities investigate whether Huang's company helped Chinese firms bypass restrictions on advanced Nvidia technology despite US export controls.

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces damage five Russian jets in strike on Savasleyka base
articles.summary: Ukraine's General Staff reported a successful strike on Russia's Savasleyka military air base, damaging three MiG-31 jets and two Su-34 fighter-bombers. The base is used to launch hypersonic missiles and bombs. The attack is part of Kyiv's long-range campaign to cripple Russian military infrastructure and energy systems following the invasion in 2022.

articles.headline: President Trump says pardon for Nvidia's Jensen Huang is an option
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that a pardon for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang remains 'always an option,' though he believes it may not be necessary. Trump claimed credit for Huang's reinstatement and urged the CEO to 'tell the truth' during upcoming congressional testimony regarding his past conduct, extramarital affairs, and security protocols.

articles.headline: US economy grows at 4.3 percent pace in third quarter
articles.summary: The US economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, the fastest in three years, according to revised Commerce Department data. Growth was driven by strong consumer spending and business investment in AI. Simultaneously, unemployment claims fell to 189,000, indicating stable labor market conditions despite higher interest rates.

articles.headline: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites for data centers
articles.summary: The FCC has granted SpaceX permission to deploy 1 million satellites for 'Starmind,' a constellation designed for space-based data centers. These orbital modules will process massive amounts of data to support global AI computing demand. The move marks a significant expansion of SpaceX's presence in the orbital infrastructure market to meet growing data processing needs.

articles.headline: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly to add safety labels to obesity drugs
articles.summary: Drugmakers Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly will add federal warning labels to obesity drugs like Ozempic and Zepbound. The move follows lawsuits from patients claiming the drugs caused permanent vision damage. The FDA now requires labeling changes to warn of potential risks related to non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) for diabetes and weight loss users.

articles.headline: Huawei convicted in US for deceiving banks over Iran business
articles.summary: A US jury found Huawei guilty of bank and wire fraud for deceiving financial institutions about its business operations in Iran. The verdict also covers the theft of trade secrets from American companies. Huawei was acquitted of racketeering conspiracy. China's government criticized the ruling, accusing the US of suppressing its companies and firm rights.

articles.headline: Trump administration shelves business-incentive plan to end Russia-Ukraine war
articles.summary: The Trump administration has reportedly set aside proposals to use corporate business deals as an incentive for Russia to end the war in Ukraine. The shift comes after Moscow showed little interest in proposed energy and aviation ventures. US envoys have informed European officials that corporate tie-ups are no longer the core pitch for ending the conflict.

articles.headline: US PCE inflation rises to 3.8 percent in October
articles.summary: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose to 3.8% in the 12 months through October, up from 3.6% in September. The data reinforces expectations that the Federal Reserve may continue raising interest rates into early 2027. Monthly prices rose 0.3%, driven by persistent underlying inflationary pressures across the US economy.

articles.headline: India faces 17% US tariff with trade deal; 25% otherwise
articles.summary: The US has proposed a tiered tariff structure for 17 countries including India. A trade deal could limit tariffs to 17% on goods like automobiles and machinery, while failure to reach an agreement could see duties rise to 25%. The move follows an investigation into industrial policies and excess capacity in several nations.

articles.headline: SEBI simplifies KYC norms to streamline investor onboarding process
articles.summary: SEBI has introduced a series of measures to simplify the know-your-customer (KYC) process by centralising information through KYC Registration Agencies (KRAs). Under the new rules, investors will no longer need to submit redundant documents to each intermediary if their data is already verified. The move aims to reduce paperwork and speed up account opening.

articles.headline: Gold and silver prices plunge on global cues, stronger currencies
articles.summary: Silver prices crashed by Rs 10,000 per kg while gold dropped by Rs 1,500 per 10g following a decline in global prices and a stronger US dollar. Gold prices fell below $2,500 an ounce globally. Analysts attribute the drop to fading geopolitical tensions and market expectations of a less aggressive interest rate cut by the US Federal Reserve.

articles.headline: Government clears Rs 2,632-crore makeover for India Post network
articles.summary: The Cabinet has approved a Rs 2,632-crore scheme to modernize the Department of Posts. The plan involves building a new transport network for faster parcel delivery and upgrading heritage post office buildings. The move aims to position India Post as a key player in the e-commerce logistics chain, particularly in rural areas through better connectivity.

articles.headline: Kamarajar Port to get Rs 4,288-cr second container terminal
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu under a public-private partnership. The project involves an investment of Rs 4,288 crore and will be executed on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Transfer basis. The expansion will significantly enhance the port's container handling capacity.

articles.headline: Imports settled in rupees surge 5-fold to Rs 2.73 lakh cr
articles.summary: India's efforts to internationalize the rupee are gaining momentum, with rupee-settled imports jumping five-fold to Rs 2.73 lakh crore in the first half of FY27. This account for roughly 7.4% of all imports, up from 1.7% in the previous year. The surge is largely attributed to increased oil imports from Russia being settled in the domestic currency.

articles.headline: Cleantech Solar to invest Rs 8,000 cr in Tamil Nadu renewables
articles.summary: Singapore-based Cleantech Solar has signed an MoU with the Tamil Nadu government to invest Rs 8,000 crore over the next five years. The company plans to develop 1.1 GW of renewable energy capacity, including solar, wind, and battery storage projects. This investment will expand their existing footprint in the state and support green energy goals.

articles.headline: India’s equity market capitalisation crosses Rs 500 lakh crore milestone
articles.summary: India’s total equity market capitalisation has crossed the Rs 500 lakh crore mark for the first time. This growth is driven by a massive surge in domestic investors and mutual fund assets, which have reached Rs 83 lakh crore. SEBI officials noted that the number of demat accounts has nearly six-folded over the last decade, reflecting deep financialization.

articles.headline: Anthropic brings Claude Duet AI work agent to India
articles.summary: AI startup Anthropic has announced the launch of its Claude Duet research preview in India. Claude Duet is designed as an AI work agent that can perform complex tasks, draft documents, and manage workflows for professional users. The service will be available across desktop and mobile platforms, aiming to enhance productivity for Indian businesses and developers.

articles.headline: Uncertainty over Parliament winter session draws criticism from Opposition
articles.summary: Opposition parties have criticized the government for the lack of clarity regarding the dates for the winter session of Parliament. Leaders like Kapil Sibal and K.C. Venugopal alleged that the delay is a violation of constitutional processes and intended to avoid accountability. The government is yet to announce the schedule, which usually starts in late November.

articles.headline: EV financing emerges as key growth driver for NBFC sector
articles.summary: Non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) are seeing a significant surge in electric vehicle (EV) financing, which is outpacing growth in the overall auto loan portfolio. During the recent festive season, EV retail sales jumped 52% year-on-year. Improved charging infrastructure and a wider range of affordable models are driving consumer confidence in the segment.

articles.headline: ISMA pegs sugar output lower than government estimates for 2026-27
articles.summary: The Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) has projected sugar production for the 2026-27 season at 26.5 million tonnes. This is lower than the government’s estimate of 27.5-28.5 million tonnes. The lower forecast is attributed to varying rainfall patterns and crop damage in major producing states like Maharashtra and Karnataka.

articles.headline: Sooryavanshi record double century eyes Asia Cup victory for India A
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored a record-shattering 204 in the Asia Cup Rising Stars contest against the UAE. Following a 30-minute motivational call with idol Yuvraj Singh to fix technical flaws, the young dasher helped propel India A. The team now prepares to face Sri Lanka in the semifinal today, looking for a collective performance to secure a final berth.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot secures first coalition deal to form Israeli government
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has reached a milestone by clinching a coalition agreement with bloc ally Avigdor Liberman. This marks the first formal pact in his efforts to form a government with only ten days left on his mandate. Liberman is reportedly attempting to draw ultra-Orthodox allies away from Benjamin Netanyahu’s 53-seat bloc to reach the 61-seat majority.

articles.headline: UP man arrested in West Bengal after 17 years for robbery
articles.summary: A 54-year-old man from Meerut, Shaukat Ali, was arrested in North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, by a joint team of Uttarakhand STF and Dehradun police. Wanted for 17 years in multiple robbery cases across Uttarakhand and carrying a reward of Rs 1 lakh, Ali had been living under a concealed identity working as a tile fitter. He faces 11 criminal cases registered in UP and Uttarakhand since 1991.

articles.headline: Two Indians injured in Houthi strike on Riyadh financial district
articles.summary: India has condemned a Houthi attack on a Riyadh financial district tower that injured two Indian nationals on November 24. The Ministry of External Affairs described the strike as a violation of Saudi Arabian sovereignty and a threat to regional security. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh is providing assistance to the injured families while reiterating firm solidarity with the Kingdom.

articles.headline: PM Modi pitches classroom to career approach for ITI students
articles.summary: Chairing a PRAGATI meeting, PM Narendra Modi urged Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to strengthen links with Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). He advocated for a 'Classroom–Company–Career' model to bridge the gap between skilling and employment. Chief secretaries have been challenged to establish specialized clusters across states and UTs within the next three months.

articles.headline: Kerala passenger arrested for mid-air assault on IndiGo flight
articles.summary: Roshan Martin was arrested at Kochi airport for allegedly punching and attempting to strangle a fellow passenger with a belt during an IndiGo flight from Abu Dhabi. The victim, 50-year-old Yusuf, sustained eye injuries. The altercation occurred 35,000 feet in the air, prompting cabin crew intervention. Martin has been remanded in judicial custody under sections for voluntarily causing hurt.

articles.headline: Investigation launched into missing rice truckloads worth 4 crore in MP
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh authorities are investigating the disappearance of 32 truckloads of rice, exceeding 1,000 quintals, that never reached destinations in Indore and Neemuch. The consignments from Katni have been missing for over a year. Minister Govind Singh Rajput has ordered a probe into suspected pilferage or illegal diversion, warning of criminal prosecution for negligent officials.

articles.headline: Madras HC rejects transgender devotee PIL for Sabarimala temple entry
articles.summary: The Madras High Court refused to entertain a PIL filed by a transgender devotee alleging denial of entry to the Sabarimala temple. The court suggested the petitioner approach the Kerala High Court, noting that since the individual was personally affected, the plea could not be maintainable as a Public Interest Litigation. The bench questioned the petitioner's locus standi in Tamil Nadu.

articles.headline: Woman arrested for slow-poisoning family with lead in Ghaziabad
articles.summary: Renu Bhatnagar was arrested for allegedly spiking the food of her husband, son, and nephew with small doses of lead over 12 months. The husband, Sushil Kumar Bhatnagar, discovered the poisoning after medical tests showed high lead levels in his blood. Police believe the woman sought full control over the family's transport business, which has a Rs 6 crore annual turnover.

articles.headline: Maharashtra soyabean harvest crashes 56% due to August rainfall deficit
articles.summary: Soyabean output in Maharashtra is estimated at just 21.2 lakh tonnes, a sharp 56% drop from last year's 48.4 lakh tonnes. Despite an expanded sowing area of 50.6 lakh hectares, low rainfall during the critical pod formation stage in August and September led to crop failure. Experts warn this will severely impact farmer incomes in Marathwada and Vidarbha and strain village economies.

articles.headline: Arunachal villagers defiantly reject proposed Siang dam project
articles.summary: Residents in Upper Siang district, Arunachal Pradesh, have boycotted meetings with central and state officials regarding the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. Despite Home Minister Amit Shah's promises of development and strategic security from Chinese dams, local leaders declared they would rather be 'cut into pieces' than abandon their ancestral homes and lands for the project.

articles.headline: Clerics apologize after Vande Mataram controversy at J&K Waqf event
articles.summary: Muslim clerics who attended a J&K Waqf Board function in Srinagar issued a public apology after the national song Vande Mataram was played in full. The national song triggered religious controversy in Kashmir. The clerics stated they did not endorse the song and sought repentance before Allah. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju attended the event, where all six stanzas were played per protocol.

articles.headline: Yogi Adityanath says AI tool identified crore Hindu voter deletions
articles.summary: UP CM Yogi Adityanath defended his claim that over 1 crore Hindu voters were deleted from state electoral rolls, stating the figure was derived using an AI tool. He rejected allegations of communal politics, asserting that under BJP, welfare benefits reach everyone regardless of caste. He also criticized Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed visit to the Ram Temple.

articles.headline: Jharkhand Assembly resolution seeks halt to electoral roll revision
articles.summary: The Jharkhand Assembly passed a resolution demanding a suspension of the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The resolution cited procedural hurdles and spelling mismatches that made 38% of the electorate 'doubtful'. Finance Minister Rameshwar Oraon alleged the current process risks disenfranchising genuine voters, including tribals, women, and migrant workers.

articles.headline: Congress launches pan-India 'Samvidhan Raksha March' against vote theft
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge will lead a nationwide 'Samvidhan Raksha March' starting today in Lucknow. The campaign targets alleged 'vote chori' and lack of transparency in the Election Commission's processes. Party leaders urged citizens to join the march to protect democratic rights, framing the issue as a fight to ensure India remains a democracy of 'We, the People'.

articles.headline: Allahabad HC rules unreserved category open to all on merit
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court quashed the preliminary results of the 2025 assistant prosecution officer (APO) exam, ruling that the unreserved category cannot be exclusive to general candidates. The court held that meritorious reserved category candidates must be adjusted into the unreserved pool at every tier of recruitment. UPPSC has been directed to hold the Mains exam afresh based on this.

articles.headline: MP High Court slaps 60k cost on DGP over accident payout
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court imposed a litigation cost of Rs 60,000 on the Director General of Police for opposing compensation awards for victims of a police bus-SUV collision. The court rejected all six appeals by the DGP, which argued contributory negligence by the SUV driver without proof. The court partially allowed victim petitions seeking higher compensation for the fatal April 2024 crash.

articles.headline: Drugs return as central poll issue in Punjab as elections loom
articles.summary: Twelve years after becoming a major political topic, the drug menace has returned to the forefront of Punjab's political discourse. The BJP-SAD alliance has announced a December 2029 deadline to eliminate 'chitta' (drugs), targeting the ruling AAP for failing its 2022 promises. The issue remains a significant challenge for a state labeled with an infamous tag since the 2016 film Udta Punjab.

articles.headline: Murder accused out on bail shot and attacked outside Pune court
articles.summary: Five assailants fired at Mandar Kiwale, a 36-year-old murder accused, outside the Shivaji Nagar district court in Pune before attacking him with billhooks. Kiwale, recently released on bail, is in critical condition. Police captured the five suspects after an 85km chase near Daund. Preliminary findings suggest the attack was retaliation for a murder committed in Katraj last year.

articles.headline: Meta officials meet Congress over suspended opposition social accounts
articles.summary: Meta executives met with Congress social media head Supriya Shrinate following complaints of bias and the suspension of over 54 lakh youth-related posts. Shrinate raised concerns that the company acts as a 'political agent' by removing opposition-related content. Meta officials argued they are bound by Indian laws to take down posts within three hours of a government request.

articles.headline: Tiger Shroff shooting case: Accused found to be minor
articles.summary: A special court has directed that a 17-year-old boy arrested in connection with the Tiger Shroff shooting case be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board. The court found he was a minor at the time of the October 19 incident when gunmen fired at the actor's vehicle in Juhu. Twelve other accused remain in custody for the attack that saw the minor spend 37 days in adult detention.

articles.headline: Three people trampled to death by elephants in separate Assam attacks
articles.summary: Three people, including a daily-wage worker guarding crops, were killed in separate elephant attacks in Assam's Tinsukia, Jorhat, and Charaideo districts. The toll from similar incidents in the region has reached five in one week. Residents are demanding solar-powered electric fencing and regular patrols as elephants stray from sanctuaries into tea estates and paddy fields in search of food.

articles.headline: TIFR plans 11-storey academic building on Colaba campus
articles.summary: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) is planning its first major academic expansion in nearly 40 years. An 11-storey building will be constructed on the 15-acre Colaba campus to house various departments. The project aims to address a long-pending need for additional research and academic infrastructure for the premier science institution.

articles.headline: Supreme Court slams slow-paced arbitration as worse than civil litigation
articles.summary: The Supreme Court expressed disappointment over the state of arbitration in India, calling it 'worse than civil litigation' due to long delays and high fees. The bench highlighted a 2019 dispute where arbitration fees reached Rs 13 crore over seven years without resolution. The court urged retired judges serving as arbitrators to introspect on maintaining the credibility of the institution.

articles.headline: MEA issues show-cause notice to Sourav Das over passport info
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs has issued a show-cause notice to CJP co-convener Sourav Das regarding discrepancies in his place of birth on his passport. Das has been advised not to use his passport until he submits a response. He was recently stopped from travelling to the UK. Das moved the Delhi High Court on Wednesday to challenge the travel restriction.

articles.headline: Bangladesh seeks Hasina's extradition from India via diplomatic channels
articles.summary: The Bangladesh government has announced it is pursuing the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from India through formal diplomatic channels. Asserting that her Awami League party will never be allowed back into politics, officials stated that legal processes are being initiated to bring her back for trial following her departure during recent national unrest.

articles.headline: Australia passes Online Safety Law with multi-billion dollar fine risks
articles.summary: Australia’s parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Act, requiring tech giants to proactively reduce online harms. Non-compliance could result in fines up to 5% of a company’s global revenue. While supporters call it a landmark for child protection, the US government and Australian opposition warned the law could lead to the censorship of lawful speech.

articles.headline: US Democrats clinch House majority with 259 seats
articles.summary: House Democrats have secured a significant majority of at least 259 seats in the 435-member US House, their best general election result since 1990. This outcome sets up a divided government with a Republican president and a Democratic-controlled Senate. Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda focused on living costs and oversight of the incoming Trump administration.

articles.headline: Thomas Markle indicted on child pornography charges in California
articles.summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been indicted by a California grand jury on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse images. Prosecutors allege FBI agents found 35mm negatives and slides in storage facilities in Los Angeles and at his former residence in the Philippines. Markle, 82, is currently in custody in Florida for violating house arrest conditions.

articles.headline: GTA VI fans outraged by emphasis on romance and chores
articles.summary: Fans of the Grand Theft Auto franchise have expressed anger over a new honor system in GTA VI that reportedly rewards good deeds and discourages wanton violence. Critics on social media accuse the developer of bowing to 'feminist slop' by emphasizing healthy living, household chores, and buying flowers for girlfriends over the series' traditional gameplay elements like killing sprees.

articles.headline: Denmark guidelines ban prosecutors from wearing headscarves in court
articles.summary: The Danish government has introduced rules requiring prosecutors to appear religiously and politically neutral in court, which includes a ban on wearing headscarves. The move follows a 2018 ban on full-face Islamic veils in public. Activists argue that such bans curtail women's freedoms, while the government debates extending headscarf bans to schools and universities.

articles.headline: US Army detonates 5 tonnes of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
articles.summary: The US Army intentionally detonated its entire five-tonne stockpile of degraded lead azide at an Iowa ammunition plant. Officials warned the material was too unstable to move and posed an explosion risk as temperatures cooled. Residents within 8 kms were urged to evacuate due to lead dust concerns, though the EPA reported no immediate lead detection in the air following the blast.

articles.headline: Bangladesh wage hike for garment workers falls short of demands
articles.summary: Bangladesh has approved a 36% minimum wage hike for garment workers, raising monthly pay to $138. The increase is the smallest in four decades and fell far short of worker demands for 32,000 taka ($257). The decision triggered fresh clashes between police and workers in Gazipur, a major manufacturing hub, as security forces used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters.

articles.headline: 11 Indians killed in UAE bus accident after truck collision
articles.summary: Eleven Indian nationals were killed when a bus carrying 41 passengers rammed into a parked truck in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Four victims were from Kerala, with others from Punjab, UP, Rajasthan, and several other states. The passengers were returning from Oman after completing visa change processes. The bus was owned by a Kerala-based travel company.

articles.headline: KMF reduces Nandini curd price by Rs 2 per kg
articles.summary: Following public backlash over a steep hike earlier this month, the Karnataka Co-operative Milk Producers’ Federation has announced a Rs 2 per kg price cut for Nandini curd. The 1kg pouch will now cost Rs 66, and the 500g pouch Rs 33, effective November 29. However, milk prices, which rose by Rs 8 to Rs 12 per litre, remain unchanged, leading to criticism from the hotel industry.

articles.headline: Chemistry emerges as second most popular subject in CBSE Class XII
articles.summary: CBSE registration trends for the 2027 Class XII board exams show Chemistry as the most popular elective after English, with 10.8 lakh registrations. Candidate numbers in Chemistry have grown 70% in eight years, far outpacing commerce subjects like Accountancy and Business Studies. The trend highlights a growing gap between core science and commerce subjects among senior secondary students.

articles.headline: Police seize 5.7kg of MDMA hidden in vanity bag in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Yelahanka New Town police arrested a car mechanic and a woman for allegedly peddling 5.7kg of MDMA. The drugs were concealed in the lining of a vanity bag to avoid detection. Suspicious of the bag's weight, officers sliced it open to find the contraband. The duo reportedly received the consignment in Delhi and drove back to Bengaluru to supply smaller peddlers.

articles.headline: Minister pulls up engineers over child-unfriendly 'step pavements' in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda criticized civic engineers for building high 'step pavements' instead of slopes, making them unusable for children and the elderly. He instructed the BBMP and other city corporations to ensure continuity of footpaths and install bollards to prevent vehicles from parking on them. Around 2,300km of city roads are slated for asphalting by February.

articles.headline: Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road realigned to spare Lalbagh garden
articles.summary: Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda announced that the proposed Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel road will be realigned to avoid Lalbagh botanical garden following citizen protests. Despite the win for the garden, MP Tejasvi Surya reiterated opposition to the entire project, alleging it will still impact 3.3 acres of Hebbal Lake and is unnecessary for traffic management.

articles.headline: Organisers cancel Pakistani drama screenings in Bengaluru after social media backlash
articles.summary: Private screenings of Pakistani television serials scheduled for November 28 and December 5 in Bengaluru were cancelled by the hosts. The Bloom Society Sisters’ Club cited 'careful consideration' following intense social media backlash and warnings from police about potential protests. The venues, including a private theatre and a restaurant, distanced themselves from the events.

articles.headline: Karnataka expands HPV vaccination drive for 15-year-old girls
articles.summary: The state government has expanded its HPV vaccination drive in mining-affected areas to cover 15-year-old girls in addition to 14-year-olds. The modification aims to align with national goals and prevent cervical cancer in districts like Ballari and Tumakuru. The drive, funded by the Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Corporation, covers 10 specific taluks.

articles.headline: NITI Aayog review finds PLI hiring lags behind industry investment
articles.summary: A NITI Aayog review of the Rs 1.9 lakh crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme shows that while companies have met 76% of investment targets, job creation is at only 28%. Sectors like solar panels and battery-cell manufacturing are seeing major infrastructure growth but minimal hiring. High-tech sectors received the bulk of incentives, while food processing led in job targets.

articles.headline: India women's hockey team tops Asian Champions Trophy league standings
articles.summary: The Indian women's hockey team secured a 4-0 victory over Japan to finish the league stage of the Asian Champions Trophy with a perfect record of five wins. The win, powered by goals from Lalremsiami and Deepika, helped India rise to a best-ever World No. 4 ranking. India finished the standings with 15 points, having recently defeated Olympic silver medallists China.

articles.headline: South Africa crushes Bangladesh for 2-0 Test series sweep
articles.summary: South Africa defeated Bangladesh by an innings and 219 runs in the second Test to complete a 2-0 series sweep. Wiaan Mulder was the hero, scoring a century and taking a career-best seven-wicket haul for 31 runs. Bangladesh was dismissed for 91 and 184 in their two innings, failing to cope with Mulder and the South African pace attack at Centurion.

articles.headline: IOA set for major makeover with nine executive council exits
articles.summary: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) is heading for a significant leadership shift as nine prominent members, including president PT Usha and AIFF chief Kalyan Chaubey, are missing from the draft nominations for 2026-30. The changes come amid a governance crisis and pressure from the IOC to resolve administrative gridlock ahead of India's 2030 Commonwealth Games hosting plans.

articles.headline: Yuvraj Singh confirms life biopic is on track for 2027
articles.summary: Former cricketer Yuvraj Singh confirmed that a biopic on his life journey, covering his career highs and his battle with cancer, is expected to start filming next year. Singh expressed a desire for a 'normal and honest' portrayal. While the final cast is undecided, he mentioned Ranbir Kapoor and Vicky Kaushal as potential leads to bring his inspiring story to the big screen.

articles.headline: Marathi film Gondhal and Naga drama Angh eligible for 2027 Oscars
articles.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has listed Marathi film 'Gondhal' and Nagaland-set drama 'Angh' among 104 titles eligible for consideration at the 2027 Oscars. Gondhal is India’s official submission, while Angh secured eligibility after winning at the Toronto International Film Festival. Both will now compete in the preliminary round of voting for the shortlist.

articles.headline: Nifty eyes record peak as FIIs buy large-cap stocks
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 surged nearly 1.9% to close at 25,819.25, driven by ₹3,485 crore in net buying by foreign institutional investors. Gains were led by banking and FMCG sectors. While benchmarks are approaching all-time highs, analysts suggest the rally may face volatility and consolidation. A stronger rupee and lower Brent crude prices below $90 a barrel supported the positive market sentiment.

articles.headline: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang returns as CEO after board exit
articles.summary: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO 11 days after the board voted for his exit following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. His return raises concerns about the influence of single individuals on Big Tech firms. While investors are relieved, the firm still faces law enforcement charges related to alleged chip smuggling and faces stricter regulatory scrutiny over AI export controls.

articles.headline: Ajit Doval addresses eighth Colombo Security Conclave in Male
articles.summary: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval emphasized collective capacity building to deal with evolving security challenges during the Colombo Security Conclave in Male. He reiterated India's commitment to working closely with member countries to enhance regional security. The conclave serves as a platform for maritime security, anti-terrorism, and cybersecurity cooperation in the Indian Ocean.

articles.headline: India faces water crisis as groundwater levels drop into stressed zone
articles.summary: India is heading toward a water crisis due to overexploitation of groundwater and heavy dependence on seasonal rainfall. Per capita water availability fell into the 'stressed' zone in 2011 and is projected to drop to 83% of 2021 levels by 2051. Experts suggest the country needs urgent policy resets to manage water scarcity as demand for agriculture and urban consumption continues to rise.

articles.headline: India reclaims top emerging market rank in October
articles.summary: India overtook Vietnam to secure the top spot in Mint’s Emerging Markets Tracker for October. Despite trailing on five of seven high-frequency indicators, India edged ahead due to a substantial lead in import cover and a narrower gap in exports and currency performance. India’s GDP growth remains a structural advantage at 7.8%, though elevated inflation remains a concern for the outlook.

articles.headline: Naveen Jindal prioritizes low debt over rapid steel capacity expansion
articles.summary: Jindal Steel chairman Naveen Jindal stated the company will grow at a conservative pace to avoid significant debt. Unlike JSW Steel's plan to double capacity by 2031, Jindal Steel will focus on raw-material security and increasing capacity to 21 million tonnes by 2032. The cautious approach follows a near-bankruptcy in 2016, with the firm now aligning expansion with its financial strength.

articles.headline: US proposes extra tariffs up to 25 percent on Indian goods
articles.summary: The US proposed new tariffs of up to 25% on India and other nations following a probe into manufacturing policies that allegedly hurt American commerce. The duty could drop to 17% if a bilateral trade deal is signed. The US is India's largest export market, receiving $87 billion in goods in FY26. India remains committed to trade talks and maintains it has no structural overcapacity.

articles.headline: Cross-border insolvency rules unlikely to be finalized this fiscal
articles.summary: The government is unlikely to rollout the cross-border insolvency framework this fiscal year as it parses stakeholder concerns. Fears exist that defaulters might use the rules to shop for friendlier foreign courts to disadvantage domestic lenders. The framework is intended to help Indian creditors access overseas assets of debt-laden firms, but requires safeguards to prevent procedural misuse.

articles.headline: Black Friday weekend becomes significant sales driver for Indian malls
articles.summary: Indian shopping malls are expecting a 15-20% increase in sales during the Black Friday weekend, which now accounts for up to 30% of monthly store revenue. Mall operators report higher footfalls and average spending across categories like fashion, beauty, and jewellery. Retailers are using the discount-led event to drive consumption beyond the traditional festive season and year-end sales.

articles.headline: PLI Auto disbursements surge to 4,385 crore rupees in FY27
articles.summary: The Centre has disbursed ₹4,385 crore under the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto parts so far this fiscal year. This brings cumulative payouts under the ₹25,938 crore scheme to ₹6,771 crore. The acceleration in disbursements signals growing manufacturing activity and investment in the sector since the incentive programme began payouts in fiscal year 2025.

articles.headline: India sugar production likely to decline 5 percent in 2026-27
articles.summary: India's gross sugar production is estimated to drop 5% to 26.52 million tonnes in the 2026-27 marketing year due to lower sugarcane output and a poor monsoon. The industry body Isma projects output will fall below the annual demand of 28.5 million tonnes. This supply gap could put additional pressure on retail sugar prices, which are already experiencing inflationary trends in the market.

articles.headline: RBI bulletin highlights India's economic resilience amid global uncertainty
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s November bulletin states that India's economic activity remained healthy in October, supported by strong consumption, credit growth, and exports. Despite geopolitical tensions and global uncertainty, high-frequency indicators suggest steady momentum. The central bank noted that domestic demand remains robust even as the global outlook for growth appears uneven.

articles.headline: India-UK investment treaty talks stall over taxation and arbitration
articles.summary: Negotiations for a bilateral investment treaty between India and Britain have stalled due to disagreements over taxation and access to international arbitration. India is reluctant to pursue a standalone pact, preferring to negotiate investment treaties alongside broader free trade agreements. The delay impacts reciprocal protections for investors in both the European and Indian markets.

articles.headline: Economists poll projects India Q2 GDP growth at 7.6 percent
articles.summary: India’s GDP growth is expected to slow to 7.6% in the July-September quarter from 7.8% in the previous three-month period, according to a Mint poll of 14 economists. A deficient monsoon and uneven rural demand are cited as primary factors for the moderation. While manufacturing and services remain resilient, agricultural growth is expected to have slumped to near-zero levels during the quarter.

articles.headline: GST e-invoicing for unregistered vendor purchases starts in 2027
articles.summary: Businesses must generate e-invoices for purchases from unregistered suppliers and overseas service providers under the reverse charge mechanism starting 1 January 2027. The move aims to improve tax compliance and create a digital trail for transactions previously not reported on an invoice-wise basis. Portals will enable voluntary generation from 15 December to help firms transition early.

articles.headline: xAI founders unveil Epochal startup to predict future events
articles.summary: Three founding members of Elon Musk’s xAI have launched Epochal, a startup aimed at teaching AI to predict future events. Its first product, a 'time portal,' allows AI agents to browse archived versions of the internet from specific dates to simulate the past. The goal is to build advanced models that assist in decision-making by understanding historical data patterns and future projections.

articles.headline: In-SPACe targets 4.1 trillion rupee revenue for private space sector
articles.summary: India's space authorization body, In-SPACe, aims to boost private space industry revenue to ₹4.1 trillion by 2033 from current levels of ₹2,000 crore. The plan involves generating demand for locally built rockets and satellites from government agencies and private firms. Isro will continue to play a foundational role while facilitating the first privately manufactured PSLV launch soon.

articles.headline: Sebi exploring AI sandbox for securities market applications
articles.summary: Sebi is exploring an artificial intelligence (AI) sandbox to test market applications in a controlled environment. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator is also examining a domestically governed AI model to make tools secure and affordable for participants. The initiative aims to foster responsible innovation and stronger cybersecurity as technology transforms financial services.

articles.headline: Foxconn faces India insolvency lawsuit over unpaid vendor dues
articles.summary: About half a dozen Indian vendors have reported payment delays by Foxconn’s local unit, with one filing an insolvency lawsuit to recover $15 million. BCD Emprasa Llp, which provided housing for Foxconn employees in Bengaluru, alleges it has not received payments for rent and utilities. The petition was filed with the National Company Law Tribunal as vendors seek to recover outstanding dues.

articles.headline: EU seeks 50 billion euros for cutting-edge frontier technologies
articles.summary: The European Union has proposed a €50 billion sovereign fund to invest in frontier technologies like AI, quantum computing, and chips. The fund aims to rival investments from the US and China by funneling public and private money into strategic sectors. The move is part of Europe's broader push to secure technological independence and maintain a competitive edge in global innovation markets.

articles.headline: Energy security risks revive investor interest in clean tech
articles.summary: India's renewable energy tech sector has attracted $722 million in funding so far in 2026, rebounding from a sharp decline last year. Growing energy security concerns following global shipping disruptions are prompting investors to back domestic generation, storage, and alternative fuels. Funding is shifting from infrastructure toward technologies that make the energy ecosystem more efficient.

articles.headline: Mizuho and Avendus Capital commence strategic financial partnership
articles.summary: Japan’s Mizuho Financial Group and India’s Avendus Capital have commenced their partnership following regulatory approvals. Mizuho Securities acquired a majority stake of over 60% in Avendus from KKR for over $500 million. Avendus will retain its brand and leadership under co-founders Gaurav Deepak and Kaushal Aggarwal as both firms aim to strengthen economic ties between Japan and India.

articles.headline: Cognizant in talks to acquire S&P Global India data team
articles.summary: IT services provider Cognizant is in negotiations to take over parts of S&P Global’s Capital IQ operations in India. The deal could move approximately 1,500 employees from S&P Global's global capability centre to Cognizant’s payroll. S&P is currently exploring strategic alternatives for its data businesses as AI drives a rethink of technology and data operations across the financial sector.

articles.headline: Corporate bond fundraising set for record high in FY27
articles.summary: Fundraising through private placements of corporate bonds has reached ₹7.16 trillion so far in FY27 and is on track to hit a record high. Companies are turning to the debt market amid tight banking liquidity and expectations of an RBI rate hike in December. Market participants expect total borrowing to surpass the previous record of ₹11.03 trillion as firms seek to lock in rates early.

articles.headline: Gold price correction sparks fresh buying for Indian wedding season
articles.summary: A 10% correction in gold prices has revived demand in India as the wedding season begins. Retailers report a 40-50% increase in sales, with customers prioritizing fresh jewellery purchases over old-gold exchanges. An estimated 5.2 million weddings are expected this season, contributing to jewelery sales of approximately ₹1.2 trillion as shoppers take advantage of the 14-month price lows.

articles.headline: Banks scrutinize data centre clients over US AI chip curbs
articles.summary: Global banks like Citigroup and Standard Chartered are reviewing Southeast Asian data centre clients to ensure compliance with stricter US export controls on AI chips. The scrutiny follows allegations of chip smuggling into China. New rules require operators in Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand to obtain licenses for advanced US silicon, threatening growth in the region's tech financing.

articles.headline: RBI compensation rules proposed for victims of digital arrest fraud
articles.summary: The RBI has proposed new rules requiring banks to compensate victims of coerced cyber fraud, such as 'digital arrest' scams. Banks may be held liable if they fail to act on warning signs or lack mandated security systems. Victims who report fraud within five days could receive full refunds or 85% compensation for losses up to ₹50,000, as regulators seek to make lenders more accountable.

articles.headline: Orchestral Qawwali Project reimagines Sufi tradition for modern audiences
articles.summary: The Orchestral Qawwali Project, led by composer Rushil Ranjan and vocalist Abi Sampa, is touring India to showcase a contemporary rendition of the 700-year-old musical genre. The project combines the spiritual essence of Sufi music with full orchestral scores and Western classical influences. The duo aims to bring the traditional rapture of qawwali to larger, global audiences through fusion.

articles.headline: Kallakurichi Police Summon TVK MLA Over IAS Officer’s Harassment Complaint
articles.summary: The Kallakurichi all-women police have served a summons on TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh regarding a harassment case. A woman IAS officer accused the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police booked the legislator under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. An IG-level officer will supervise the probe.

articles.headline: Net FDI Into India Hits Five-Year Low in September 2026
articles.summary: Net foreign direct investment into India fell to -$4.95 billion in September, marking the lowest level since at least March 2021.
